item.title: Foxconn working on new tie-up with OpenAI, says no AI bubble: Young Liu
item.description: Foxconn is exploring a fresh partnership with OpenAI, dismissing AI bubble concerns as it targets double-digit growth and expands humanoid robot deployment at its US facilities.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Foxconn, the world's biggest contract electronics manufacturer, on Friday flagged that a collaboration with leading US artificial intelligence developer OpenAI was in the works, though details were scant. Foxconn Chairman Young Liu told reporters at the company's annual event to showcase its technology that he had met OpenAI Chief Executive Sam Altman earlier in the day and there would be an announcement once details were confirmed. Liu did not elaborate further. Any deal would build upon last year's agreement between the two firms to work together on designing and engineering data-centre racks, components and other AI hardware. Foxconn, formally called Hon Hai Precision Industry and Nvidia's biggest AI server maker, is increasingly relying on AI infrastructure for growth. While AI-sector stocks have been hit hard by concerns that relentless heavy investment is not sustainable amid climbing borrowing costs, Liu said the industry was not in a bubble and that Foxconn expects to maintain double-digit growth next year. Foxconn has six factory buildings in Houston, Texas, where it manufactures AI servers for Nvidia, and sees a need for further expansion, Liu said. The company said in August that its cloud and networking products segment, which includes AI servers, accounted for 51% of second-quarter revenue, exceeding 50% for the first time.  HUMANOID ROBOTS WORKING IN HOUSTON Separately, Foxconn is making progress on plans to deploy humanoid robots at its Houston plant. Brand Cheng, chairman of unit Foxconn Industrial Internet (FII), told Reuters on Friday that more than 10 humanoid robots had been deployed at its Texas facilities for internal use. Foxconn plans to extend deployment beyond Texas, he added. According to presentation materials seen by Reuters, FII introduced two wheeled models in October — one that lifts things vertically and one that can bend at the waist for assembly as well as loading and unloading tasks. The unit is developing AI models for humanoid robots based on Nvidia's GR00T foundation model.

item.title: Nvidia in talks to give credit support for Nscale's deal with Anthropic
item.description: Nvidia is reportedly considering billions of dollars in credit guarantees to help Nscale finance a West Virginia AI data centre for Anthropic, though the deal has not been finalised.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Nvidia is in talks to offer AI cloud provider Nscale billions of dollars in credit guarantees to support debt funding for a data center earmarked for Anthropic, The Information reported on Thursday, citing people with knowledge of the talks. The credit support would help fund power infrastructure and construction of Nscale's AI data centre in West Virginia, which Anthropic plans to use, according to the report. Nvidia is an investor in the UK-based cloud provider. The deal has not been signed and terms could still change, the report said. Nvidia, Nscale and Anthropic did not immediately respond to Reuters requests for comment. Claude maker Anthropic struck a deal in August to spend $45 billion to rent computing power from Nscale's West Virginia data center campus. Nscale is also in talks to sell about 460 megawatts of AI computing power to Anthropic in another deal that could also be worth about $45 billion. The report comes as companies such as CoreWeave and Firmus, which are both backed by Nvidia, have been hit by concerns about debt financing behind the AI build-out.

item.title: Jio Platforms Q2 profit rises 13.7% to ₹8,387 crore, revenue up 11.4%
item.description: Jio Platforms reported a 13.7% rise in Q2FY27 net profit to ₹8,389 crore, marking its first quarterly results since the telecom and digital major's record $3.2 billion stock market debut.
item.content:encoded:
Home / Companies / Quarterly Results / Jio Platforms Q2 profit rises 13.7% to ₹8,387 crore, revenue up 11.4%

Jio Platforms Q2 profit rises 13.7% to ₹8,387 crore, revenue up 11.4% JPL IPO broke records across all investor categories; a milestone for the next growth phase: MD Akash Ambani

The company listed on the BSE on October 28, raising Rs 30,188 crore in what was termed India's largest public offering

Gulveen Aulakh New Delhi 6 min read Last Updated : Oct 30 2026 | 11:38 PM IST

Listen to This Article

Jio Platforms Ltd (JPL), the parent company of India’s largest telecom-services provider Reliance Jio, on Friday reported a net profit of ₹8,389 crore for July-September 2026-27 in its first earnings report after its blockbuster market listing earlier this week.     Net profit was up 13.7 per cent from ₹7,379 crore in the same period last financial year.   Revenues rose 11.4 per cent to ₹40,475 crore from ₹36,332 crore the same quarter last year.   In the previous quarter, profits were ₹7,764 crore and revenues ₹39,173 crore. The company raised ₹30,188 crore in what is India’s largest initial public offering. Also Read

“We were raising ₹30,000 crore-odd, and we saw demand of over ₹7.5 trillion. We saw every investor category broken, starting from QIB (qualified institutional buyers) to small HNI (high net worth), big HNI, retail, and all the various shareholders, employees, all of the categories were broken,” said Akash Ambani, managing director, JPL, at the analyst call following the results.

The top executive at India’s second-largest company by market capitalisation said that JPL’s IPO numbers came at a time when the Indian markets had seen outflows of more than ₹48,000 crore, led by foreign portfolio investors.   “In a market situation like that, (we are) very proud that the people (are) realising (what) business we’ve built ... we put in extremely hard work over the last 10 years to build this business, and we’ll continue to do so,” Ambani noted, adding, the IPO was a new milestone, and that the company would move on from here.   “We believe that you know the value that we can create over the next decade or so is even more than what we have done in our first decade, and we’ll continue to aspire to that perspective,” he said.

Quarterly earnings before interest tax, depreciation and amortisation climbed 16.6 per cent year-on-year to ₹21,879 crore. The 250-basis point rise in margins was driven by revenue growth and operating leverage.   Jio reported average revenue per user (Arpu), a monthly metric of profitability of a telecom services provider, at ₹218.8, marginally up from ₹215.6 in Q1FY27. However, year-on-year, Arpu was up 3.5 per cent, from ₹211.4, on the back of promotional schemes for fixed broadband customers and increased usage.   “We warmly welcome our new shareholders to the Jio Platforms family as we enter a new era as a listed company. This quarter’s results continue to reflect the strength of our 5G network, and the growing reach of our broadband and digital services,” Ambani said in a statement to the exchanges.

The company said in its statement to the stock exchanges that ₹27,500 crore from the net proceeds from the IPO has been used to prepay, in full or in part, the principal amount outstanding of the external commercial borrowing of Reliance Jio Infocomm Ltd, a material subsidiary of JPL, and the balance amount would be for general corporate purposes. JPL’s net debt reduced by 78.6 per cent to ₹8,822 crore from ₹41,161 crore in Q2FY26. Debt reduced quarter-on-quarter by 7.5 per cent from ₹9,539 crore in Q1FY27.   Finance costs rose 40.3 per cent to ₹3,009 crore, up from ₹2,145 crore in Q2FY26.

Reliance Jio ended September 2026 with 542.4 million users, including 300 million 5G subscribers. The carrier added 9.1 million subscribers during the quarter.

Jio’s 5G data traffic in the fourth quarter reached 71.3 billion gigabytes, while total voice traffic rose 1.3 per cent to 1.52 trillion minutes. It added 66 million 5G customers over the last 12 months, and 15 million over the past quarter. Customer engagement also remains robust with data consumption at 44.2 GB per month, higher than 38.7 GB per month in the same period last year.   Fixed broadband subscribers as of September 2026 stood at 30 million with about 7.3 million additions over the last 12 months.

Jio AirFiber had over 15.1 million subscribers, driving more than 75 per cent of the fixed broadband additions during the last 12 months, the company said. “Ahead of the curve investment on next generation technologies has been the foundation of Jio’s success over the past decade. We would continue to build our capabilities across satellite communications, 6G intellectual property and AI embedded in our core voice and data services as we create lasting value for all our stakeholders,” Ambani added. He elaborated the company’s strategy, noting that it was unlike a traditional telecom services provider owing largely to its proprietary technology with integrated 4G, 5G stack, unlicensed broadband radio (UBR) and now fixed wireless becoming 50 per cent of its base.

He added that Jio would double down on offers to the enterprise because it would be a major growth opportunity, with India having 350,000 lease lines.    On expanding internationally, Ambani said that the company would be “very selective” about the markets that it would go to.   “We will not be selling our proprietary stacks as a hardware commission … What we imagine the business model here to be is to be actually managed service partner with our customers. It’s not going to be a heavy capex rollout. You won’t see us going and putting up towers and fiber and infrastructure only. But this is something that we think that will be enabled because of the only proprietary stack that we have," he added.

Stating the company’s competitive advantage — owing to full-stack technology across seven layers, deep engineering and proprietary IP contribution — Ambani said Jio had multiple growth engines across mobility, home, enterprise, and international.   “We are the ones that have a clear path of growth and profitability improving with a very strong balance sheet, even before the IPO proceeds come to us,” he added.      ALSO READ:  RIL's O2C Ebitda jumps 68% on higher fuel cracks and chemical margins

item.content:encoded:
Home / Markets / Commodities / Oil prices rise on supply concerns as Houthis attack Saudi Arabia

Oil prices rise on supply concerns as Houthis attack Saudi Arabia Brent crude futures rose 86 cents, or 0.75%, to $115.74 a barrel as of 0122 GMT while US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude futures rose 72 cents, or 0.71%, to $102.72

For the month, Brent was on course to finish nearly 14% higher, while WTI was heading for a 15% jump to close above $100 for the first time since April

Reuters SINGAPORE 2 min read Last Updated : Oct 30 2026 | 8:45 AM IST

Listen to This Article

Oil prices climbed in early trade on Friday on supply concerns after Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis stepped up attacks on Saudi Arabia, on track for a fourth straight monthly gain and the steepest since July. Brent crude futures rose 86 cents, or 0.75%, to $115.74 a barrel as of 0122 GMT. US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude futures rose 72 cents, or 0.71%, to $102.72. For the month, Brent was on course to finish nearly 14% higher, while WTI was heading for a 15% jump to close above $100 for the first time since April. On Thursday, the Houthis said they had attacked several sites in Saudi Arabia, including its largest oil refinery, Ras Tanura, the Rabigh refinery and an Aramco facility in Abqaiq, while a Saudi-led coalition said it had intercepted a cruise missile launched by the Houthis towards the kingdom's western region.

"Continued kinetic action around the Strait of Hormuz amidst doubts of a viable diplomatic pathway are keeping oil prices elevated in expectation of an escalation of the conflict in coming weeks," said MST Marquee Head of Energy Research Saul Kavonic. Also Read

US President Donald Trump said on Thursday that Vice President JD Vance had reached out to Iran to help the country get medical supplies, after US media reported Vance had written to Tehran's top security official to revive peace talks. Iran has received a letter from Vance but it has not responded to it yet, the country's semi-official Tasnim news agency reported, while adding that Tehran wants the US to meet its conditions and "any position that contradicts this framework is unacceptable."

Meanwhile, Iran's Revolutionary Guards said three tankers hit sea mines, exploded and caught fire while attempting to use an unauthorised route south of the Strait of Hormuz. Amid security concerns in the region, ExxonMobil and Chevron have cancelled plans for their executives to travel to the United Arab Emirates' biggest oil show next week, two sources familiar with the developments told Reuters.

(Only the headline and picture of this report may have been reworked by the Business Standard staff; the rest of the content is auto-generated from a syndicated feed.)
